newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens stronger in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens stronger in light trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3728 (US$0.7284) in light trading on Monday as the unit continued to consolidate ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, dealers said. * They said the Canadian dollar should show a positive bias this week with the release of economic data likely showing a buoyant economy.
"With Tokyo closed, volume was a little thinner than usual," said one trader with a Canadian bank.
The trader said the Canada dollar would take its initial direction from the release of retail sales data due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
A Reuters forecast of economists predicted a 0.6 percent increase for May compared to a 1.1 percent increase in April.
Traders said calls for an interest rate hike in Canada, which moved markets on Friday, had been largely discounted in the market. "It's a move that is completely unfounded," the trader said.
The central bank raised its key bank rate by 25 basis points four weeks ago in an attempt to shore up a weak Canadian dollar.
"We won't see a rate hike this summer unless there is some unexpected and dramatic weakening of the Canadian dollar," said Steve Saldanha, economist with Canada Trust Investment Management.

Saldanha said it was possible that Canada could see two or three Bank of Canada rate hikes by the beginning of 1998, but not until the Bank has a sign that unemployment is heading below the 9.0 percent level.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3067 marks from 1.3029 marks at Friday's close and jumped to 84.31 Japanese yen from Friday's 84.06 yen.
